entities.summary: Aurelius Valerius Symmachus Tullianus (b. 250 CE, Rome) was a Roman senator and administrator of the Late Roman Empire. He served as consul in 361 CE and was known for his diplomatic efforts to maintain the Empire's borders. Symmachus was a skilled orator and wrote a treatise on Roman law, 'The Twelve Caesars', which remains an important source for understanding the Late Roman Empire. He was a key figure in the debates over the use of the altar of Jupiter at Rome, which was a symbol of imperial power and religious identity. Symmachus's legacy can be seen in the continued use of Roman law and the importance of diplomacy in maintaining imperial borders. His writings provide valuable insights into the complexities of Roman politics and society during this period. As a prominent figure in the Eastern Roman Empire, Symmachus played a significant role in shaping the imperial administration and maintaining the Empire's stability. He was a key player in the negotiations between the Roman Empire and the Sassanid Empire, which had significant implications for the region's politics and economy.
